cases.sentence: Старик сидел один за столом, в туфлях и в ___, и просматривал для развлечения, без большого, однако, внимания, какие-то счеты.
cases.explain: «старом пальтишке» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Alyosha went in. The old man was sitting alone at the table wearing slippers and a little old overcoat. He was amusing himself by looking through some accounts, rather inattentively however. He was quite alone in the house, for Smerdyakov too had gone out marketing. Though he had got up early and was trying to put a bold face on it, he looked tired and weak. His forehead, upon which huge purple bruises had come out during the night, was bandaged with a red handkerchief; his nose too had swollen terribly in the night, and some smaller bruises covered it in patches, giving his whole face a peculiarly spiteful and irritable look. The old man was aware of this, and turned a hostile glance on Alyosha as he came in.

cases.translation: He said this with almost hostile feeling. At the same time he got up and looked anxiously in the looking-glass (perhaps for the fortieth time that morning) at his nose. He began, too, binding his red handkerchief more becomingly on his forehead.

cases.sentence: Так вот я теперь и подкапливаю все побольше да побольше для одного себя-с, ___ мой Алексей Федорович, было бы вам известно, потому что я в скверне моей до конца хочу прожить, было бы вам это известно.
cases.explain: «милый сын» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “He doesn’t ask for money, it’s true, but yet he won’t get a farthing from me. I intend living as long as possible, you may as well know, my dear Alexey Fyodorovitch, and so I need every farthing, and the longer I live, the more I shall need it,” he continued, pacing from one corner of the room to the other, keeping his hands in the pockets of his loose greasy overcoat made of yellow cotton material. “I can still pass for a man at five and fifty, but I want to pass for one for another twenty years. As I get older, you know, I shan’t be a pretty object. The wenches won’t come to me of their own accord, so I shall want my money. So I am saving up more and more, simply for myself, my dear son Alexey Fyodorovitch. You may as well know. For I mean to go on in my sins to the end, let me tell you. For sin is sweet; all abuse it, but all men live in it, only others do it on the sly, and I openly. And so all the other sinners fall upon me for being so simple. And your paradise, Alexey Fyodorovitch, is not to my taste, let me tell you that; and it’s not the proper place for a gentleman, your paradise, even if it exists. I believe that I fall asleep and don’t wake up again, and that’s all. You can pray for my soul if you like. And if you don’t want to, don’t, damn you! That’s my philosophy. Ivan talked well here yesterday, though we were all drunk. Ivan is a conceited coxcomb, but he has no particular learning … nor education either. He sits silent and smiles at one without speaking—that’s what pulls him through.”

cases.sentence: — Вот ты говоришь это, — вдруг заметил старик, точно это ему в ___ только в голову вошло, — говоришь, а я на тебя не сержусь, а на Ивана, если б он мне это самое сказал, я бы рассердился.
cases.explain: «первый раз» — after the preposition «в», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “There! you say that,” the old man observed suddenly, as though it had struck him for the first time, “and I am not angry with you. But if Ivan said it, I should be angry with him. It is only with you I have good moments, else you know I am an ill-natured man.”

cases.sentence: С тобой только одним бывали у меня добренькие минутки, а то я ведь ___.
cases.explain: «злой человек» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.

cases.sentence: А услышит если сегодня, что тот меня до полусмерти, ___, избил, так, пожалуй, бросит его, да ко мне придет навестить…
cases.explain: «слабого старика» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “If I send the ruffian to prison, she’ll hear of it and run to see him at once. But if she hears that he has beaten me, a weak old man, within an inch of my life, she may give him up and come to me. … For that’s her way, everything by contraries. I know her through and through! Won’t you have a drop of brandy? Take some cold coffee and I’ll pour a quarter of a glass of brandy into it, it’s delicious, my boy.”

cases.sentence: — Вот таких-то эти ___ и любят, кутил да подлецов!
cases.explain: «нежные барышни» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “There you see how dearly these fine young ladies love a rake and a scoundrel. They are poor creatures I tell you, those pale young ladies, very different from—Ah, if I had his youth and the looks I had then (for I was better-looking than he at eight and twenty) I’d have been a conquering hero just as he is. He is a low cad! But he shan’t have Grushenka, anyway, he shan’t! I’ll crush him!”
